# Assignment for Angular Developer Position: Beech Car Maintenance

**Candidate:** BEECH KEVIN KERSTJENS [1]

## Context

A car maintenance company, "Beech Car Maintenance", wants to register the maintenance jobs it performs on various cars for various customers [1].

- Some maintenance jobs are specific to a certain brand of car or a specific model, while others apply to all types of cars [1].
- Each maintenance job has a fixed rate in terms of service hours and may require certain spare parts [1].
- Spare parts can be generic for almost all cars, or specific per brand/model (e.g., many cars share the same engine block) [1].

## The Assignment

According to the class diagram, write modern Angular code that calculates the total price for servicing a car (i.e., the price for an instance of `ScheduledMaintenanceJob`) [2].

**Guidelines:**

- You may not need to implement all of the classes in the diagram [2].
- You are allowed to add extra classes if necessary [2].
- Use best practices for writing Angular applications [2].
- Make sure your code runs on the latest version of Angular [2].

### Calculation Requirements

Your price calculation must keep track of the following aspects [2, 3]:

- Maintenance servicing hours performed on the weekend cost more than maintenance during weekdays [3].
- Spare parts have different costs based on the type of the part [3].
- Each type of maintenance job has a fixed rate in terms of service hours [3].
- Sum up spare part prices and servicing hours [3].
- Calculate VAT [3].

### External System Integration

Write code that fetches the actual, current price of spare parts from an external system at the car manufacturer [3]. This price should be fetched in real-time and used in the total servicing price calculation implemented above [3].

## Additional Deliverables

- **Assumptions:** Make a list of all assumptions you made that were required for completing this assignment [4].
- **Code Comments:** Use a reasonable level of comments in your code so others will be able to maintain it [4].
